selection_caveat: Both studies examine AIR-affiliated channels; membership selection, missing/inactive/nonmonetized publishers and participant overlap across AIR studies prevent platform-wide inference.

studies.selection: 300 AIR-affiliated monetized channels, 10,000 to 50 million subscribers across 13 niches; only monetized months
studies.audience: YouTube view events on selected channels; unique people not measured
limits: Overall median belongs to selected AIR client channels and monetized months, not all video views or all YouTube owners.
RPM already expresses creator revenue per thousand views after the platform share, but is not cash profit or income per work hour.
Niche sample sizes are unreported in displayed table; starred niches have fewer than ten channels and must be flagged directional.
Do not use the observed 300-channel median to estimate creator labor productivity, platform-wide success or newcomer earnings.

studies.selection: AIR client channels across 13 niches; 127 channels supplied monetized streaming revenue/subscriber monthly observations
limits: The 404 total channels and 127 monetized live channels are different analysis populations.
1,287 channel-months are repeated measurements, not independent channels, a unique viewer count or streamer population.
45 is the study's median livestream view-count measure in monetized streaming months, not a median creator income or all livestreams.
Within-channel streaming/nonstreaming comparisons are observational with seasonality and upload effort confounding, not a universal causal streaming effect.

cross_study_deduplication.method: Do not add 300 and 404 to assert 704 unique channels. Obtain anonymized sample IDs and consented cross-study overlap data first.
